items.actClause: AN ACT to direct the division of criminal justice services to promulgate rules and regulations relating to residences of certain sex offenders
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S4890

TITLE OF BILL:  An act to direct the division of criminal justice
services to promulgate rules and regulations relating to residences of
certain sex offenders

PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:  The purpose of the bill is to require
the division of criminal justice services to create and disseminate
rules and regulations to clarify which agency is responsible for enforc-
ing distance restrictions for the proposed residences of sex offenders,
as well as establish a uniform standard of measurement for determining
said distance restrictions.

SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1, subsection 1, of the bill requires the division of criminal
justice services to promulgate rules and regulations that are necessary
to clarify the agency that is responsible for enforcing the distance
restrictions for proposed residences of sex offenders who are subject to
the laws which restrict their presence within 1,000 feet of school
grounds, including but not limited to specific instruction on how the
responsible agency may enforce such restrictions.

Subsection 2 requires the establishment of a uniform standard of meas-
urement for determining distance restrictions, including parameters to
be used, such as measurement from the "real property line boundary" of
school grounds and include clarification of the area of the proposed
residence that is to be used in determining the distance, including but
not limited to, offenders on parole and on probation.

Section 2 provides that this act shall take effect immediately

JUSTIFICATION:  After shelters across the state were recently revealed
to be housing large numbers of convicted sex offenders, serious concerns
were raised about the implementation of the current residency
restriction laws In order to address these enforcement issues, this bill
aims to direct the division of criminal justice services to clarify two
main points: the agency who is responsible for the enforcement of resi-
dency restriction laws and the standard of measurement used to determine
the '1000 feet' distance.

PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:  None

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS:  None.

EFFECTIVE DATE:  This act shall take effect immediately.

A.actClause: AN ACT to amend the executive law and the penal law, in relation to the requirement for certain sex offenders who are on probation or parole, or conditionally released to reside certain distances from school grounds
A.lawCode: Add 259-f, Exec L; amd §220.00, Pen L
A.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S4890A

TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the executive law and the penal law, in relation to
the requirement for certain sex offenders who are on probation or
parole, or conditionally released to reside certain distances from
school grounds

PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

The purpose of the bill is to establish a uniform standard for
measuring and enforcing the 1,000 feet restriction between school
grounds and sex offender residences.

SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 of the bill would require the department of corrections and
community supervision, in consultation with the board of parole,
director of probation and correctional alternatives, and division of
criminal justice services (DCJS), to establish a uniform standard for
measuring and enforcing the 1,000 feet distance restriction between
proposed residences for registered sex offenders and school grounds.
The standard and methodology for measuring the distance must be posted
on the website for DCJS for the public to view.

Section 2 provides that for purposes of measuring the beginning and
end points of the 1,000 feet residence restriction, the beginning and
end points shall be measured from the closest point of the real
property boundary line of the school grounds to the closest point of
the real property boundary line of the sex offender's proposed
residence. This would exclude any real property portion of the sex
offender's residence or any real property portion of the school
grounds from being counted within the 1,000 feet restriction.

Section 3 provides that this act shall take effect immediately

JUSTIFICATION:

Currently, various criminal justice state entities, such as DOCCS,
DCJS, the Board of Parole, and Office of Probation and Correctional
Alternatives all have some level of involvement with released sex
offenders. After shelters across the state were recently revealed to
be housing large numbers of convicted sex offenders, serious concerns
were raised about the implementation of the residency restriction
laws. In order to address these enforcement issues, this bill
clarifies that the department of corrections and community supervision
is responsible for measuring and enforcing the 1,000 feet residence
restriction laws relating to sex offenders, in consultation with other
state agencies. This would clarify which criminal justice agency is in
charge of measuring and enforcing the residence restriction.

In addition, the bill clarifies the beginning and end points for
measuring the 1,000 feet distance between the school grounds and sex
offender's residence.

PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:


None

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS:

None.

EFFECTIVE DATE:

This act shall take effect immediately.

summary: Directs the commissioner of corrections and community supervision to establish standards for the distance certain sex offenders on probation or parole, or conditionally released, must reside from school grounds.
title: Directs the commissioner of corrections and community supervision to establish standards for the distance from school grounds of the residence of certain sex offenders on probation or parole
